interest: Shows pre-war land scarcity and wartime food crisis in Japan, tracked from Swiss intelligence on crop shortages.
overview: Decimal file 894.61 (spanning April 1941 through June 1944) comprises U.S. diplomatic reporting, research memoranda, and wartime economic intelligence concerning Japanese agriculture, rural economics, and food supply policies before and during World War II. The pre-war documentation includes consular dispatches from Shanghai on Japanese government monopolies over vegetable oils and Manchurian soybeans, as well as Division of Far Eastern Affairs analyses of Dr. Shiroshi Nasu's landmark monograph 'Aspects of Japanese Agriculture', highlighting extreme land scarcity, tenant farming, and rural poverty. The wartime records consist of intelligence cables dispatched from the U.S. Legation in Bern, Switzerland, monitoring Axis press reports and Tokyo broadcasts to assess Japan's deteriorating food situation, diminished rice harvests, and emergency state initiatives promoting the cultivation of substitute staples such as potatoes, wheat, and barley.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a supplementary memorandum on Japanese vegetable oil control regulations to accompany an annual agricultural policy report.
subfiles.from: Frank P. Lockhart, American Consul General, Shanghai
subfiles.summary: Lockhart forwards a supplement on Japan's vegetable-oil controls, omitted from an earlier agricultural-policy report, plus notes on further studies underway.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 408 from Shanghai transmitting supplement on Japanese agricultural policy

subfiles.about: Summary of Japanese imperial ordinances establishing state control companies for the purchase, importation, and distribution of soybeans and vegetable oils.
subfiles.from: Agricultural Attaché, American Consulate General, Shanghai
subfiles.summary: Memo: Japan's 1940 ordinances gave state monopolies control over soybean and vegetable-oil purchase and marketing.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Control of Vegetable Oil in Japan
subfiles.to: Frank P. Lockhart, American Consul General, Shanghai

subfiles.about: Detailed review and statistical extraction of data on land tenure, tenancy, and farm income from Dr. Shiroshi Nasu's monograph.
subfiles.from: Cabot Coville, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Coville summarizes Nasu's study of Japanese agriculture: tiny dwarf farms, 46.5% tenancy, slowing population growth, and low farm income compared to the US.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Cabot Coville reviewing Shiroshi Nasu's 'Aspects of Japanese Agriculture'
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Adviser on Political Relations

subfiles.about: Routing slip requesting that the Division of Far Eastern Affairs review Dr. Shiroshi Nasu's study for information of interest.
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Adviser on Political Relations
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck asks Far Eastern Affairs to review Nasu's agricultural study for relevant material.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Stanley K. Hornbeck requesting review of Nasu's study

subfiles.about: Formal acknowledgment of receipt of a complimentary copy of Shiroshi Nasu's monograph from the Institute of Pacific Relations.
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Adviser on Political Relations
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck thanks the Institute of Pacific Relations for sending Nasu's study of Japanese agriculture.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to the Institute of Pacific Relations

subfiles.about: Intelligence report from Japanese publications detailing food shortages, crop shift initiatives, and agricultural quotas for 1943-1944.
subfiles.from: Leland Harrison, U.S. Minister to Switzerland, Bern
subfiles.summary: Harrison reports Japan's 1941-43 food shortages from poor rice harvests, prompting a push for substitute crops like potatoes and wheat with raised purchase prices.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1995 from Bern on Japanese food situation and crop planning

subfiles.about: Intelligence cable relaying a Tokyo broadcast estimating that the 1944 European potato harvest fell short of wartime targets.
subfiles.from: Leland Harrison, U.S. Minister to Switzerland, Bern
subfiles.summary: Harrison reports Japan's 1944 potato crop estimate rose over 1943 but still falls short of the government's quota.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 3959 from Bern on Japanese European potato crop estimates

subfiles.about: Intelligence report citing German press coverage of Japanese wheat and barley crop estimates for 1944.
subfiles.from: Leland Harrison, U.S. Minister to Switzerland, Bern
subfiles.summary: Harrison reports Japan's 1944 wheat and barley harvest rose to 27 million koku on better weather and more acreage.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 3947 from Bern on Japanese wheat and barley crop estimates
